tips.comment: Useful Flat racer (by Sea The Moon) trained by Joseph O'Brien. Pecked a few hurdles on his way to success at 1-4Fav last week at Newton Abbot. Might do the same here but can again come out on top. The opposition doesn't have comparable form.

Should not reverse placings with today's hot favourite Dignam on last weeks run @ Newton Abbot. However, interesting that connections want to take the Irish hotpot on again here and very good jockey/trainer combination makes current 16/1 the Ew play in the race.

The model I run suggests Keel Strand can win this one. Keel Strand lines up here with the highest RPR of the 8-horse race but hasn't been penalized for it in the weights. Has the joint lowest official ranking and subsequently steps out carrying significantly less weight than the other 7 runners. Won the previous 3 on the spin and so comes here in red-hot form. Hopefully, stepping up here in class isn't enough to prevent 4 times on the spin. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

The model I run suggests Midnight Jewel can win this one. Midnight Jewel lines up here with a comparably high RPR and has an official ranking that leaves it closer to the lower order in the weights. Midnight Jewel also comes here in good form, having got the job done when last out 26 days ago. Wheeled out again in quick order, prior distance winner, and looks in good shape to take it to two wins on the bounce.

Raby Mere has been a revelation since joining Olly Murphy, winning twice and placing second on his other two appearances. He only just failed at Perth last time, so we could have been looking at a three time winner. This is his first run over fences, but the trainer is very adept at switching his horses between disciplines. He's only six and there can be more to come.
Aslukwoodhavit changed yards last month and showed improvement when second up and dropping from C2 to C3. More improvement is expected now dropping to C4.

I can't help think that they've been feeling their way with this one. Never really put into the race in the rear over C&D recently, which was his first appearance since a wind procedure. A 3lb ease in the ratings can only help and it would be great if they would let him fly like in Ireland as he's sitting on an attractive mark.

A useful chaser at his peak, but no longer has the strength of his earlier days and has recently been competing in hunter chases. He has shown pleasing performances in his last 2 outings, but has work ahead of him here. He gives away age and weight to his competitors, yet the McCain stable should not be underestimated. The odds of 11/1 present good value for an each-way wager on this veteran.

I am surprised that this isn't closer to favourite. He had too much to do when finishing second behind a subsequent winner over 2m here LTO, who actually beat a subsequent winner himself. A 4lb rise is lenient and I think reverting to this longer trip will bring an improved performance too. Sixty Plus is up 15lb and well worth taking on, while La Quarite is far from certain to prove as effective over hurdles.

The model I run suggests La Quarite can win this one. La Quarite lines up here with the second highest RPR of the 12-runner field but has an official ranking that is second last. This leaves La Quarite stepping out carrying the second lowest amount of weight around this 2m 3f handicap hurdle. La Quarite has shown signs of good form, with figures of 2-4321, with that latest win coming only 7 days ago. Turned out again in quick succession to take advantage of the form, and race fitness shouldn't be a concern. The model has issued a 'low' stake indicator driven by a combination of the mid-sized gap back to second and the reasonable odds on offer at 3.5s. This translates to a 0.75pt bet on a scale of 0-4.
Dropped into an easier race and running off correct rather than the 3lb OH in the better race last time. He performed well and comes into this in good form.
In the best form of his career winning well over course and distance last time out. The 10 lbs increase might not be enough to stop him achieving the hat-trick here.

Could potentially be let in lightly here, having only been raised 4 lbs for the dominant success last time out, even if the other runners did underperform. A mark of 134 asks a new question, however, as does the trip he's running over. Plus, he's in here off the back of a break. He did place off a 1 lb lower mark at Aintree last season, so not exactly handicapped out of things here. He boasts 4 wins from 9 runs over fences. The trainer boasts a healthy strike rate with chasers running at this track. The tongue tie and cheekpieces are tried again. His form figures sporting that combo read 21. If he's fit from his break, he's got claims in this competitive handicap chase.

The model I run suggests Harry's Hope can win this one. Harry's Hope lines up here with a comparably high RPR to the other runners in this 8 horse contest, but has an official ranking that leaves him rock bottom in the weights. Sets out carrying 1 stone 10 lbs less to the top weight and Ben Jons picks up the reins. Harry's Hope has shown some signs of form with figures of 2P-212, so knows how to get close at the business end of the race. Will need to show more to go close here today. Model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.
Bluebella changed yards in May, and the latest two runs are showing improvement. Both were second, with the latest only missing out by ¾L, and could still improve again while just 2 lbs heavier.
Won well at Worcester returning from a wind operation last time out. Can overcome the 5 lbs increase and follow up here.

This horse has finished 4th in his last two runs. In both races, he ran a little freely. Both races were over today's distance, and if kept in behind a few horses, I fancy this horse can go very close.
Has had a good run the last few months, winning three, two in quick succession. Made mistakes last time out. Has been favourite in her last five races. Chance here at a bigger price.

Has been running well in this class since winning @ Sedgefield 4 runs back and that includes over C/D Lto. Retains that mark of 88 here, good conditional retains ride taking off 7lb and shrewd dual trainer is 24 percent with his hurdlers here last 5 seasons, making current 18/1 worth Ew consideration in the race.

Open-looking mares' hurdle. Donald McCain's team is in decent order right now (3 winners from the last 18 runners). Lady Buttercup has shown some ability. Won a mares' bumper less than a year ago. Third on penultimate start, only beaten 3.5 lengths before running too freely last time. First-time hood applied now. Looks well handicapped.

Drops back a couple of grades. Dropped 1lb for the last run, which in fairness was much better than the finishing position would suggest. He's now 1lb lower than his last winning mark (over hurdles). He won a better race than this one, winning a class 3 at Plumpton, pulling clear of the runner-up. He won on the flat at Chelmsford on his penultimate run, winning very easily despite racing wide. He put 4L between himself and the runner-up. He ran well in a class 2 handicap last time out, despite finishing 6th. He was only beaten 5L by the winner. He's a perfect 3/3 at this track. This race is weaker than the races he's been contesting lately. He should be going close here.

Ten length winner of a bumper for Ross O'Sullivan before joining this yard. Brought along slowly since but travelled strongly before winning first handicap hurdle outing (a Class 5 at Stratford) off a mark of 98 earlier this month. Gavin Sheehan retained for trainer Jamie Snowden. Up five pounds for that win but receives weight from many here. Going the right way and looks to have a decent chance of success.

The model I run suggests Gavin can win this one. Gavin lines up here with a comparably high RPR in this 10-horse race but has over 1 stone and a half less in weight to carry than the top weight and current market leader, Lelooopa. This kind of weight difference over the 2m trip can be telling by the finish line. Shane Fenelon on board relieves a further 5 lbs, which is helpful, but so too do other jockeys riding, so the impact is nullified. Gavin has shown signs of some form lately with figures of 16242 and is a prior course and distance winner. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator, which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

Olly Murphy's 7yo is pretty consistent over both hurdles & fences & goes well for Lewis Edmunds , who is good value for his 7lb claim. My only worry is him getting in a battle for the lead, as there's one or two headstrong characters in the field. If he's sensible & lies up in second or third, he'll take the beating.
No comment made
This horse comes into this race in good form. It has placed 3rd and won in his last two runs, both 3-mile handicaps at Perth. The drop in trip could well be ideal for this horse today.

The model I run suggests a big upset from Leading Lion is the value bet. Leading Lion lines up here with the highest RPR by quite some way and has an official ranking that leaves it looking well treated in this company. Hasn't shown any great form of late and has been pulled a few times, but is a prior distance winner here over this 2m 3f. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.
Point Lynas is a course and distance winner at Pontefract and was ahead of Prague when finishing a close 2nd last time in a Group 2 at Ascot and should confirm the form.
Win only bet on Prague here as some of the other horses look regressive, whereas I feel Prague has a few more gears. I think it looks like a false favorite here.
Make Me King won in listed company last December in Abu Dhabi and returned from a break last month to a close third in a G3. So, he should be fit, and I always expect more when second up.

Going through a barren run as it's now been 14 runs since the last win back in 2023. But he has put up some solid performances this year that should give him some confidence. So with that in mind, I think he represents good value.
Eeetee won here in June off a 64 and bounced back off a 66 last week under Jack while claiming 5 lbs. He goes again off the same mark but with Jack claiming 7 lbs this time.
Second last time, winner at Beverley. Distance no problem. Jockey and trainer in form. Great each way bet at 10/1. Shortlist Mmaterial, will be there at the finish. Nap Each Way.

Arkenstaar is a well-handicapped five time winner whose best form has historically come at Hamilton, but he's shown signs he could strike elsewhere. His latest effort at Ayr saw him finish 7th, beaten only 4 lengths in a race where he raced wide from a double-digit draw. He now drops into a Class 5 contest off OR 77, returning to Pontefract where he's not been disgraced. With Connor Beasley back on board and conditions in his favour, he looks capable of outrunning his odds.
I like a few in the race, and Eeetee comes in as a solid favorite. But with the allowance and a couple of good runs under its belt and in decent times, I'm willing to take a punt each way.

Super Hit is a 4-year-old who has shown he can be effective off this mark, having scored over 7f off 66 back in April at Musselburgh. He ran respectably when fourth at Beverley last time, beaten 6 lengths in a race that may not have suited him tactically. He has won once and placed once from five runs at this distance and goes well enough on similar ground. Jason Hart takes over in the saddle, and trainer Darryll Holland keeps the tongue strap on, which has been worn for all three career wins. From stall number 3, he has a handy draw, and with 18 runs under his belt, a 17% win and place rate, he is not badly treated and has definite chances if bouncing back. The pace is likely to be solid, which suits his usual mid-pack style also.

Charming Princess was beaten a head last time at Ffos Las by a William Haggas-trained colt and has a valuable newcomer from William Haggas to worry about here. But the colt that beat her at Ffos Las had finished 2nd twice himself and had sufficient experience. Sea The Stars colt Golden Horse may need a run to show his best, especially on a tricky course like Pontefract.
A solid 4/14 at Carlisle after being off for just over a year, with the promise of more to come this time, puts him into the place claims category.

A very good horse on its day and largely consistent, although it needs a race to fall into place. Although with a small field, I fancy it to outrun its odds off bottom weight. The Actor, a saver, was very good, fallen right off, but could surprise.
No comment made
Yet to win this season but had been running well until a below-par effort at Newcastle last time. Needs to put that behind her but has slipped to the last winning mark, so should run well.

This race is very weak, and with a small field of horses, it may pay to side with top weight Bosh. The handicap mark has fallen to 83 after a long losing run but has been running in some tough handicaps and in better class. Showed signs of a return to form last time but was ultimately well beaten, finishing 4th. A return to turf and good ground at Pontefract should bring on more improvement.
Not firing on all cylinders just yet, but only one win from 10 runs to date. I think fortunes will change for the new yard, now helped with a dropped mark and a 5lb claimer.

Chairmanfourtimes has to overcome a wide draw at Pontefract but likes to go with the pace and could come across early towards the rail with a smart start and his previous form suggests he should come out on top this time.
Cloudbuster did a grand job when third up in a C4 at 6f last time out but lost second in the last 100 yds. So worth a shot back at 5f today.
Shown some good early season form, but had a poor run lately when never a factor from a poor draw. Gets a better draw today and looks well in at weights. Trainer's only runner on the card.

Made a promising debut in a class 5 novice over 5f @ Beverley, when keeping on very well to come 5/11 beaten 4.5 lengths. Entitled to come on for that run/experience, this stiff 5f will suit and good jockey/trainer combination makes current 22/1 decent Ew here.

A Time Test filly. She is a half-sister to the capable winner Diligent Resdev, who has excelled up to 7f, as well as the 7f winner Nammos. Her dam, while not having raced, comes from the lineage of the notable 8.5f winner Absolute Crackers. The yard has a strong history with debut runners, and with the jockey in good shape, an each-way bet at 25/1 presents a fair opportunity.

Raulin looks solid here with the allowance. Has run a poor last couple of races but has had excuses. 10f looks a good distance, draw also good. Believe this will be a start to finish race. Small saver on Looks Fantastic.

A beaten favourite over this trip at Ayr under today's jockey off a mark of 75 beat a length into third place back in May 2025. Disappointed in a big field at York next time out and the soft ground would not have suited at Ayr last time out. This better ground should suit more and could go well off this mark of 72 against this opposition.

A very capable, yet inconsistent performer who, on his day, goes very well. 3rd at Beverley early this month, then an off-the-pace 7/9 at York a week later. Oisin Orr in the saddle looks positive. Hope he is on a good day; if so, he can win this.
Off since January and missed the whole of 2023, so relatively lightly raced for an 8-year-old and well in on old form. Worth an each-way nibble.
Won over 7 furlongs 10 days ago off a mark of 46 beating horses ranked in their 50's and can defy a 3 pound rise to follow up.

Filey Beach is being tried over a sprinting distance for the first time after a promising first run for Ruth Carr, in which he raced prominently over seven furlongs at Thirsk, weakening into 4th in the last half furlong. Although one pound out of the handicap here, he raced off 46 to 48 all last season and finished 2nd twice in September and October. He probably needed his run at Thirsk after a break of 206 days.

Veteran, who hasn't won for a while, has been running fairly consistently so far this season and posted a solid effort when 2nd at Hamilton last time. Been raised a lb for that but should still run well this afternoon.
Won his penultimate race in a classified race over the distance. Last race was over a mile and was competitive for three-quarters of the distance. Back down in trip for today.

Flavius Titus might be getting on a bit but did win this last year off a 50. I think that today's mark of 46 and having Rowen Scott back in the saddle, who was on top for that last win, could see a revival on the return here. EW 4P.

Mick Easterby trained 3yo filly by Soldier's Call. Hasn't shown much yet but finally coming down the handicap. Pontefract might suit much better. The trainer does quite well here. Lewis Chalkley claims a 7lbs allowance.

Too Bossy For Us is very much the first string of the two Willie Mullins-trained horses here. Patrick Mullins rides (Grand National winning jockey). The selection is a four-year-old by Derby and Arc Winner Golden Horn. Ran second of 25 to a stablemate at a very similar staying trip to this at the Curragh recently. Beaten favourite that day, but it was a strong effort. Up a few pounds but still looks to hold a good chance in this company. Good horses down the years, but they look a bit jaded compared to this clearly progressive 4yo who ran very well on sole Flat start for this yard so far (won a Class 3 at Ascot when with Kevin Philippart De Foy). Worth backing at odds of 5-1.

Plontier is another that is getting on a bit, but the last win in August was after a break. Although a bit duff since, the last two runs in December and January were in a G2 and a G1. It's worth an EW shot while back in handicap with 5P on offer.
